# posthog_event_schema (Resource)

Attach a `posthog_schema_property_group` to an event. The event must have been ingested at least once so its event definition exists. Schema management is currently observational: attached schemas describe the expected shape but do not reject non-conforming events at ingestion until PostHog enables schema enforcement.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "posthog_schema_property_group" "checkout" {
  name = "Checkout"

  properties = [
    {
      name          = "cart_value"
      property_type = "Numeric"
      is_required   = true
    },
  ]
}

# The event must have been ingested at least once so its definition exists.
resource "posthog_event_schema" "checkout_completed" {
  event             = "checkout_completed"
  property_group_id = posthog_schema_property_group.checkout.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `event` (String) Name of the event to attach the property group to (e.g. `checkout_completed`).
- `property_group_id` (String) UUID of the `posthog_schema_property_group` to attach.

### Optional

- `project_id` (String) Project ID (environment) for this resource. Overrides the provider-level project_id.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Timestamp when the event schema was created.
- `event_definition_id` (String) UUID of the event definition the event name resolved to.
- `id` (String) UUID of the event schema attachment.
- `updated_at` (String) Timestamp when the event schema was last updated.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import using: project_id/event_schema_uuid
terraform import posthog_event_schema.checkout_completed 12345/your-event-schema-uuid

# If project_id is configured at the provider level, you can omit it:
terraform import posthog_event_schema.checkout_completed your-event-schema-uuid
```
